newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: P.Morris bid for Tabaqueira would add jobs.
newsitem.headline: P.Morris bid for Tabaqueira would add jobs.

text.p: A joint bid for Portuguese state cigarette manufacturer Tabaqueira by Philip Morris of the U.S. and Portugal's Jorge de Mello group will create additional jobs and production, a source linked to the bid said.

The Philip Morris/Mello bid, competing against two others, foresees the creation of 100 new jobs, a new shift at Tabaqueira's factory at Albarraque near Lisbon and an increase in annual production to 21 billion cigarettes by 2001 from 10 billion now, said the source.

"If we win the bidding for Tabaqueira, Philip Morris plans to transfer immediately the production of all its brands to the Tabaqueira factory at Albarraque, which would become our manufacturer and distributor for southern Europe," said the source, who asked not to be identified.
The three bidders are competing to control a 65 percent stake of Portugal's biggest tobacco company. The winner should be known next month.
The joint bid by holding PMM-SGPS, representing Philip Morris and the Jorge de Mello industrial group, offered 5,100 escudos per share for Tabaqueira, valuing the stake at 33.15 billion escudos.

The two other bids are from Spanish firm Tabacalera, in partnership with Portugal's Empresa Madeirense de Tabacos, which offered 5,610 escudos per share, valuing the stake at 36.465 billion escudos, and French firm Seita, which offered 4,800 escudos per share, valuing the stake at 31.2 billion escudos.
